faq.title: The questions people ask us before downloading

items.question: How long does a parcel take to arrive?
items.answer: The length of the flight, plus the time it takes to agree a meeting with the recipient. You see the traveller's departure and arrival dates before you book: you are the one choosing the trip that suits you. We do not advertise a standard delivery time, because there is no delivery round behind it: there is a flight, taken by a real person.

items.question: How much does it cost to send something?
items.answer: The traveller sets their price per kilo according to their route and what they agree to carry. yadony adds 12% on top. For a 5 kg parcel with a traveller charging €12 a kilo: €60 for them, €7.20 commission, €67.20 for you to pay. The full breakdown is on the Pricing page.

items.question: What am I not allowed to send?
items.answer: Cash, jewellery, identity documents, medicines, perishable food, narcotics, weapons, and anything the customs rules of the destination country prohibit or restrict. The traveller opens the parcel in front of you at handover: they take on the liability by carrying it in their own luggage, so they have the right to know what they are carrying.

items.question: When am I charged?
items.answer: You are only charged after delivery. When the traveller accepts your parcel, your payment method is registered; the charge itself happens only once the delivery scan has been validated by the recipient, and it is that same scan that triggers the payout to the traveller. If the parcel never leaves, or never arrives, nothing is taken from you.

items.question: What if the parcel never arrives?
items.answer: You open a dispute from the app. The payout to the traveller stays suspended while the case is examined. We go back through the scan history, which shows the last validated step, at what time and with which photo. If the loss is established, the payment is not charged and the traveller receives nothing. The value you declared, capped at €500, is the reference amount for the case: it is not a promise of compensation on our part.

items.question: How much does a traveller earn?
items.answer: Exactly the price they advertised. The 12% commission is added on top and is paid by the sender: it is not taken out of what the traveller receives. Ten kilos at €12 a kilo means €120 paid out after delivery, on a ticket already bought.

items.question: What happens if there is a customs check?
items.answer: The traveller declares what they are carrying. In the app, every parcel comes with a description and the photos taken at handover, which they can show. Any duties and taxes remain payable by the sender. That is also the reason for the list of prohibited items: a parcel held up at customs holds up the person carrying it.

items.question: Which cities are covered?
items.answer: Departing from Paris, Lyon and Marseille, to Dakar, Abidjan, Bamako and Douala. These are the corridors with enough flights and enough people for the service to hold up from day one. Others will follow. We would rather open a city when it works than show a map full of destinations with no travellers on them.

seo.title: How to send or carry a parcel with yadony
seo.description: The five steps of a shipment, on the sender's side and on the traveller's side: posting, matching, scanned handover, carriage, confirmed delivery and released payment.

howItWorks.title: Two journeys, five steps each
howItWorks.lead: A shipment involves two people who do not know each other. Here is what each of them does, in order, and when the money moves.

steps.title: You describe the parcel
steps.text: Departure city, arrival city, weight, contents, photos. You declare a value, capped at €500: that is the reference amount used if a dispute has to be examined.

steps.title: You choose a traveller
steps.text: The app shows who is flying your corridor, on what date, with how many kilos free and at what price per kilo. You see their verified identity and their ratings, if they already have any. When you book, your payment method is registered: it will be charged only once delivery is confirmed.

steps.title: You hand over the parcel
steps.text: You agree a meeting point in the app. The traveller opens the parcel in front of you, scans the QR code, takes a photo. The timestamp is recorded: that is your proof of handover.

steps.title: You follow the scans
steps.text: Boarding, then arrival. Each scan sends a notification to you and to the person waiting for the parcel. A shareable tracking link lets them watch without installing the app.

steps.title: Delivery releases the payment
steps.text: The recipient receives the parcel in person, the final scan is validated, a hand-over photo is taken. That event, and nothing else, triggers the charge and the payout to the traveller.

steps.title: You post your trip
steps.text: Cities, dates, kilos available, price per kilo. You are still free to turn down a parcel without having to explain yourself.

steps.title: You go through the identity check
steps.text: An ID document and a selfie, checked by Stripe Identity. It is compulsory before you carry anything, and it is what reassures the person handing you their parcel.

steps.title: You accept a parcel
steps.text: The description, the photos and the declared value are shown to you before you accept. At handover, you open the parcel in front of the sender and scan the QR code: what you are carrying is on the record.

steps.title: You travel as usual
steps.text: One scan before boarding, another on arrival. The parcel goes in your luggage, within the allowance granted by your airline.

steps.title: You deliver and you get paid
steps.text: Hand-delivery, final scan, photo. The payout is triggered straight after. You receive the full price you set: the 12% commission is paid by the sender, on top.

We do not claim to replace them: for a bulky, urgent or high-value shipment, they remain the right choice. For a few kilos that someone close to you is waiting for, the price question no longer looks the same.

seo.title: Trust and safety: verified identity, escrow payment, disputes
seo.description: How yadony secures a shipment between private individuals: Stripe Identity verification, payment charged only after delivery is confirmed, declared value capped at €500, dispute procedure and data handling.

trust.title: What the platform guarantees, and what it does not
trust.lead: This page describes the mechanisms in place, without dressing them up. If something here looks insufficient to you, write to us: it is more useful to say so now than to find out when something goes wrong.

identity.title: Identity verification
identity.text: No anonymous account can send or carry a parcel. Before their first listing, every user submits an ID document and a selfie to Stripe Identity, which checks that the document is valid and that it matches the face. These documents are stored encrypted and kept apart from the rest of the database: they are never visible to other users, and internal access to them is restricted and logged. The name shown to the other party is the verified name.

escrow.title: Payment held in escrow
escrow.text: When a traveller accepts your parcel, your payment method is registered, but no money is taken. The charge happens only after the delivery scan has been validated by the recipient, and it is that scan that triggers the payout to the traveller. Until delivery is confirmed, nothing is taken from you and the traveller receives nothing. If the shipment does not go ahead, the payment request is dropped.

cap.title: Cap on declared value
cap.text: The declared value of a parcel cannot exceed €500. That cap is deliberate: above it, a shipment carried by a private individual is no longer the right channel, and a professional carrier is a better one. The declared value is the reference amount we use to examine a dispute; under-declaring it works against you. The 12% commission includes no insurance for the parcel.

tracking.title: Four scans, and the evidence that comes with them
tracking.text: Handover, boarding, arrival, hand-delivery. Each scan records a timestamp and, at handover and at hand-delivery, a photo. This history is not decorative: it is the material a dispute is examined on. It is visible to the sender and the recipient at all times, and it cannot be altered afterwards.

dispute.title: Dispute procedure
dispute.text: A dispute is opened from the app, from the moment a step does not go as planned. The payout to the traveller is suspended immediately. We examine the scan history, the timestamped photos and the messages exchanged in the app, then we decide: refund to the sender, payout to the traveller, or a split. The decision is explained and given to both parties.

data.title: Your data
data.text: ID documents are handled by Stripe Identity, stored encrypted and kept apart from the rest of the database. The other party to a shipment sees your first name, your profile photo, the status of your verification and the details of the parcel concerned — nothing more. The data for a shipment is kept as long as handling a possible dispute requires, then archived. The details are in the privacy policy.

limits.title: What we do not guarantee
limits.text: We do not carry anything: the parcel stays in a traveller's luggage, subject to whatever happens to their flight and their airline. A delayed plane, a strike or a customs check are not down to us. We do not search parcels on your behalf: it is the traveller who checks the contents at handover, and the sender who answers for their declaration. We are not an insurer either: the 12% commission includes no insurance for the parcel, and our terms commit us to no compensation amount. What we do guarantee is narrower and easier to check: the payment is not charged until delivery is confirmed, and a dispute is examined on timestamped evidence. Finally, a shipment arranged outside the app opens no recourse at all: with no scans and no payment through the platform, there is neither a record nor any leverage.

seo.title: About yadony
seo.description: Why we built yadony: the story of a problem the diaspora has been solving for thirty years in WhatsApp groups, with no record of any of it.

about.title: Why we ended up building it
paragraphs: There is one message everyone in the diaspora has written, or read: “is anyone flying to Dakar this week?”

It happens in a WhatsApp group of two hundred people. Someone answers, you swap numbers, you meet on a Saturday in a car park. You hand a box to a stranger vouched for by a cousin, you pay in cash, and you wait. Most of the time, it works. It works remarkably well, in fact: that is how clothes, school supplies, spare parts and presents have been moving for thirty years.

The problem only shows up the day it does not work. The parcel does not arrive. The number stops answering. There is no record, no proof of handover, no receipt, nobody to call. You cannot even say what happened: lost, forgotten, kept. And because the person was doing you a favour, you do not dare push. You lose the parcel, and often you lose the relationship as well.

On the other side, there are the carriers. They are reliable, they are considerably more expensive, and they do not deliver everywhere. To get five kilos to someone you know, that is not a solution, it is giving up.

yadony is not trying to replace the traveller with a lorry. The traveller already exists, is already flying, and their suitcase is already half empty. What was missing was not the transport: it was the record. Knowing who is carrying, when, and being able to prove it. Hence the identity check, the four scans, the timestamped photos, and a payment that does not move until the parcel is in the recipient's hands.

We are opening with four arrival cities, not forty, because we would rather have one corridor that genuinely works than a map that looks impressive. We have no figures to show: we are starting out. If you use the app and something strikes you as shaky, write to us. At this stage, that is the most useful feedback we can get.

seo.title: Terms of use
seo.description: The rules for using yadony: the role of the platform, identity verification, the obligations of the sender and of the traveller, price, cancellation and disputes.

cgu.title: Terms of use
cgu.intro: These terms govern the use of the yadony app and of the yadony.com site. They are accepted when the account is created and can be read again at any time from the app.

object.title: Purpose of the service
object.text: yadony connects travellers who have spare luggage space with senders who want a parcel carried. yadony is not a carrier: the company never takes possession of parcels, does not handle them and does not undertake to get them there. It provides the tool for matching, tracking and payment.

account.title: Account and identity verification
account.text: Signing up requires a verified phone number. Anyone wishing to send or carry a parcel must have completed an identity check with our provider Stripe Identity. The account is personal: it may not be lent or transferred. The information provided must be accurate and kept up to date.

sender.title: Obligations of the sender
sender.text: The sender declares the actual contents of the parcel, with no omission, and agrees to it being opened in front of them at handover. They must not send cash, jewellery, identity documents, medicines, perishable food, narcotics, weapons, or any goods whose import is prohibited or restricted in the destination country. The declared value may not exceed €500. Any duties and taxes payable on arrival remain their responsibility.

traveler.title: Obligations of the traveller
traveler.text: The traveller carries the parcel in their personal luggage, within the allowance granted by their airline. They carry out the four required scans — handover, boarding, arrival, hand-delivery — and give the parcel in person to the named recipient, with a hand-over photo. They may turn down a parcel at any time before handover, without having to give a reason.

price.title: Price, commission and payment
price.text: The price of carriage is set freely by the traveller. yadony charges a commission of 12% of that price, payable by the sender and billed in addition. The sender's payment method is registered when the parcel is accepted; the amount is charged only after the delivery scan has been validated, and the payout to the traveller follows. No charge is made if delivery is not confirmed.

cancellation.title: Cancellation
cancellation.text: The sender and the traveller may both cancel before the parcel is handed over: no amount is charged in that case. A cancellation after the parcel has been handed over falls under the dispute procedure. Repeated late cancellations may lead to a restriction on the account.

dispute.title: Disputes
dispute.text: A dispute is opened from the app. The payout to the traveller is suspended while the case is examined. yadony decides on the basis of the scan history, the timestamped photos and the messages exchanged in the app, and explains its decision to both parties. Shipments arranged outside the platform give rise to no recourse.

termination.title: Suspension and termination
termination.text: An account may be suspended for a false declaration of contents, an attempt to pay outside the platform, repeated unfounded disputes, or behaviour that puts another user at risk. A user may delete their account at any time from the app; shipments in progress must be seen through to the end.

law.title: Governing law and mediation
law.text: These terms are governed by French law. In the event of a disagreement, an amicable solution is sought first. A consumer may refer the matter free of charge to a consumer mediator before taking any legal action. Failing agreement, the dispute falls to the competent French courts.

seo.title: Privacy policy
seo.description: What data yadony collects, why, who it is shared with, how long it is kept and how to exercise your rights.

confidentialite.title: Privacy policy
confidentialite.intro: This page describes the data we process in the yadony app and on the yadony.com site, what it is used for and what your rights are. It is written to be read, not to be accepted without being read.

responsible.title: Data controller
responsible.text: The company that publishes yadony is the controller for the processing described below. Any question about your data can be sent to contact{'@'}yadony.com.

collected.title: Data collected
collected.text: Account: phone number, first name, surname, profile photo. Identity verification: ID document and selfie, sent to Stripe Identity and stored encrypted, never visible to other users and with restricted internal access. Shipments: cities, dates, weight, description and photos of the parcel, declared value, scan history with timestamps. Payments: payment details are handled directly by Stripe and never pass through our servers.

purposes.title: Purposes and legal bases
purposes.text: Performance of the contract is the basis for account management, matching, parcel tracking and payment. A legal obligation is the basis for identity verification and for keeping accounting records. Our legitimate interest is the basis for fraud prevention and platform security. Notifications unrelated to a shipment in progress rely on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time in the settings.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.text: Your data is neither sold nor rented. It is passed to our technical processors strictly as far as necessary: Stripe for payment and identity verification, our host, and our notification and SMS providers. The other party to a shipment sees only your first name, your profile photo, the status of your verification and the details of the parcel concerned.

retention.title: Retention period
retention.text: Account data is kept as long as the account exists, then deleted or anonymised. The data for a shipment is kept as long as handling a possible dispute requires, then archived to meet accounting obligations. ID documents are kept by our verification provider for the period imposed by the applicable regulations, then deleted.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You have a right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability over your data. These rights are exercised from the app settings or in writing to contact{'@'}yadony.com. You may also lodge a complaint with the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL), the French data protection authority.

cookies.title: Cookies on this site
cookies.text: yadony.com is a static site. It sets no advertising cookies, embeds no third-party trackers and loads no fonts from an external server: the fonts are served from our own domain. The language shown is determined by the address of the page, not by a cookie.

security.title: Security
security.text: Traffic to and from the app is encrypted in transit. Identity verification data is encrypted at rest and kept apart from the rest of the database. Access to the data for a shipment is restricted to the two parties involved and, in the event of a dispute, to the team examining it. Every sensitive action is logged.

what.title: What a cookie is
what.text: A cookie is a small file a website places on your device to remember information between visits. The browser's local storage plays a comparable role.

current.title: What yadony.com uses today
current.text: This site sets no advertising cookie, no third-party tracker, and embeds no analytics tool. The only information stored is your answer to the consent banner, kept in your browser's local storage.

storage.title: Duration and scope
storage.text: Your choice stays on your device until you delete it, and is never sent to our servers or to third parties. If we ever add an analytics tool, this page will be updated and your consent requested before anything is activated.

manage.title: Staying in control
